title: Close the QualityGateManager fail-open report default with a single normalization authority

defect_summary.fail_open_default: _finalize_gate read `rep.get('ok', True)`: any report dict that simply lacked an `ok` key (e.g. a status-only report or a report whose gate crashed before writing ok) was silently tallied as PASS.
defect_summary.split_authority: CumulativeGateRunner used `report.get('ok', False)` (fail-closed) while _finalize_gate used `rep.get('ok', True)` (fail-open): the SAME malformed report produced different verdicts depending on which runner evaluated it.
defect_summary.report_producers_surveyed: All 10 internal gates (dem_coverage, elevation_continuity, junction_integrity, lane_width/geometry_continuity, geometric_continuity, connector boundary, origin_sanity, elevation_seams) produce an `ok` field; structure_elevation_plausibility produces BOTH `ok` and `status`; check_external_libopendrive produces `ok` + `status` (pass/fail/skipped/error).

normalization_semantics.authority: normalize_gate_result(report) is now the single decision authority used by BOTH QualityGateManager._finalize_gate and CumulativeGateRunner.run.

rules.ok present: ok is authoritative; a co-present `status` (structure_elevation_plausibility shape) is preserved for provenance but never overrides ok
rules.status only: mapped case-insensitively onto the QualityStatus vocabulary; only PASS maps to pass. PENDING -> INCOMPLETE; GATE_TIMED_OUT -> FAIL; skipped/skip/not_run -> NOT_RUN; unrecognized status string -> FAIL
rules.no verdict key: empty or side-evidence-only reports map to FAIL (an unverified report is never an unambiguous pass)

coverage.A: _finalize_gate fails on missing verdict keys (regression: previously passed via get('ok', True))
coverage.B: _finalize_gate passes only on an explicit pass verdict
coverage.C: non-dict reports fail closed and never crash
coverage.D: status-only pass/pass and error are normalized correctly
coverage.E: PENDING -> INCOMPLETE, GATE_TIMED_OUT -> FAIL, unrecognized status -> FAIL (fail-closed)
coverage.F: runner AND manager agree on the same status-only 'skipped' report (the split-authority bug)
coverage.G: ok+status precedence: ok wins in both runners (ok True/status INCOMPLETE -> pass; ok False/status PASS -> fail)
coverage.H: empty dict fails closed in both runners
coverage.I: truthy ok coercion (bool semantics) accepted only with an explicit verdict
coverage.J: strict CumulativeGateRunner raises on a status-only evidence gap

live_impact._finalize_gate_caller_audit: All 11 in-file gate call sites feed reports that produce an explicit `ok` field; no production gate is newly failed by the stricter default.
live_impact.runner_change: CumulativeGateRunner previously defaulted missing ok to False; normalize_gate_result preserves that verdict for no-ok reports and adds status-vocabulary handling, so no behavior regression.

residual_risks: submission/infrastructure/ultimate_pipeline/quality/quality_gate_manager.py (line 56) still contains the OLD `rep.get('ok', True)` fail-open `_finalize_gate`; it is not in CRITICAL_MIRRORED_FILES and already had pre-existing drift from the canonical file, so it was left untouched. Any packaging that consumes the submission mirror instead of the canonical module inherits the fail-open defect until mirrored.

quality_gates.py still uses `.get('ok', True)` on the lane-link and external-libOpenDRIVE report paths (run_quality_gates); those use their own pass/fail routing rather than _finalize_gate. They were not changed in OC-36 (separate tape) but carry the same fail-open idiom and are recommended follow-up.
Status vocabulary is only mapped for the values enumerated in GATE_STATUS_SYNONYMS; a future producer introducing a novel status must extend that table or it fails closed by design.
